subject.title: fix(codex): refuse Platform routes on a subscription-signed native Codex home

question: Should OpenClaw fail closed for an existing user-scoped native Codex home when its selected API-key route would otherwise run under a ChatGPT subscription?
rationale: The patch deliberately changes an existing route from silent execution to an actionable refusal in order to protect an operator’s billing boundary; that upgrade behavior is a maintainer-owned product and compatibility decision.

options.title: Accept the billing guard
options.body: Merge the intentional 401 behavior after confirming it is the supported protection against API-key routes silently consuming a native ChatGPT subscription.

options.title: Preserve current behavior temporarily
options.body: Keep the existing route behavior while defining an explicit opt-in safety mode or broader migration plan for the billing boundary.

recommendation.title: Accept the billing guard
recommendation.body: Merge the intentional 401 behavior after confirming it is the supported protection against API-key routes silently consuming a native ChatGPT subscription.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the immediately preceding merged repair and this follow-up on the same user-home Codex auth contract.
